clue.text: Maxwell's line to Mirror chief: 'go downhill fast'

parts.note: Robert Maxwell, owner of the Daily Mirror, was known as Cap'n Bob, so Maxwell's is BOB'S
the chief of a newspaper such as the Mirror is its editor, ED

explanation.surface: A newspaper proprietor sends a terse instruction to his editor to make things collapse quickly.
explanation.walkthrough: Robert Maxwell owned the Daily Mirror and fell from his yacht in 1991; the clue's 'go downhill fast' hints at his fall, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To bobsled is to ride a racing sledge down an ice track at speed, which is travelling downhill fast.

clue.text: Boobs issuing report about Saudi leader

definitions.note: plural slang for breasts, matched by the collective singular noun

indicators.note: about means the report word goes round the letter

parts.note: a boom is a loud report, like a gun's

indicators.note: leader asks for the first letter of Saudi

parts.note: the first letter of Saudi is S

explanation.surface: A tabloid-style story about a Saudi ruler and breasts.
explanation.definitionFit: Bosom is a woman's chest or breasts taken together, which is what the slang boobs refers to.

clue.text: Criminal who makes a household somewhat discontented?

definitions.text: Criminal who makes a household somewhat discontented?

parts.words: Criminal who makes a household somewhat discontented?
parts.note: discontented is read as losing some of its contents, which is what a house thief does

explanation.walkthrough: 'Discontented' usually means unhappy; here it means having some contents taken away.
explanation.definitionFit: A housebreaker steals possessions, leaving the home with fewer of its contents.

clue.text: Unauthorised release didn't hold water, Mandelson explained initially to his predecessor

parts.note: a container that lets water out has leaked

indicators.note: initially asks for the first letters of Mandelson and explained

parts.note: the first letters of Mandelson and explained are M and E
Mo Mowlam was Northern Ireland Secretary before Mandelson took the post in 1999

explanation.surface: Mandelson explains to the minister before him why a leaked story didn't stand up.
explanation.definitionFit: A leaked memo is an internal document passed to the press without permission, an unauthorised disclosure.

clue.text: Removes from dormitory bed and exposes

definitions.meaning: first meaning: takes out of a bunk, as if de-bunk
second meaning: reveals something as false

explanation.walkthrough: The first meaning is a jokey literal reading: a bunk is a dormitory bed, so de-bunking removes someone from it.
explanation.definitionFit: To debunk a claim is to show it up as false or exaggerated, revealing the truth.

clue.text: To live long don't eat in this capital

parts.note: to be is to exist or live
L stands for long, as in L for longitude or a long garment size
to fast is to go without food

explanation.surface: Advice that a city's residents survive longer by skipping meals.
explanation.walkthrough: Belfast is the capital of Northern Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: Belfast is the seat of the Northern Ireland government, so it counts as a capital city.

clue.text: Pictures, on a grand scale, having an erection inside pants

indicators.note: inside means the erection word goes within the word for pants

parts.note: to pant hard is to blow, so pants gives BLOWS
in the Eye's smutty sense, an erection is something that is up

explanation.surface: Large photographs of a man visibly aroused in his underwear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pants' looks like the British word for underpants, but here it is the verb meaning gasps for breath, and 'inside' says what holds the erection.
explanation.definitionFit: Blow-ups are photographic enlargements, pictures printed at a large size.

clue.text: See 14
Key party call for what Blair would have his party be?

definitions.text: what Blair would have his party be?

parts.note: A is a musical key
a do is a party
to ring someone is to call them

explanation.surface: A swingers' key party and what Blair wants from his party members.
explanation.walkthrough: A key party is one where couples swap partners by drawing keys; Blair's party here is the Labour Party.
explanation.definitionFit: Blair wanted Labour members worshipping him, and adoring means devoted and loving.

clue.text: Frogs, some say, require the male and female to be separated in ditch

indicators.note: the pair are placed in the ditch word, which is split apart to hold them

parts.note: a trench is a ditch
HE is the male pronoun

explanation.surface: Mating frogs must be parted in a ditch.
explanation.walkthrough: Frogs is a rude British nickname for French people, and 'some say' owns up to that. 'To be separated in' means the ditch word is split to take the pair.
explanation.definitionFit: The French are mockingly called Frogs by some English speakers, a slur based on eating frogs' legs.

clue.text: Mandy's last appearance in broadcasts backing the country

indicators.note: in tells us the letter goes inside the reversed word
backing means the word for broadcasts is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: to broadcast something is to air it, so broadcasts are AIRS

indicators.note: last asks for the final letter of the nickname, the possessive aside

parts.note: Mandy is the press nickname for Peter Mandelson

explanation.surface: Peter Mandelson making a final TV appearance in support of his nation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backing' turns AIRS round to SRIA, and 'in' puts Y, the last letter of Mandy (ignoring the 's), inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Syria is a nation in the Middle East, an example of a country.

clue.text: Minister is aware, it's said, of how to humbly sniff an opening

parts.note: Gordon Brown was the government minister in charge of the Treasury at the time

indicators.note: it's said means the word is spoken aloud and spelt differently

parts.note: someone who is aware of something knows it, so KNOWS

explanation.surface: A government minister knows how to grovel to get a foot in the door.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It's said' tells you KNOWS is heard as NOSE. The definition is the Eye's crude take on what flattering someone involves.
explanation.definitionFit: To brown-nose is to flatter servilely; the vulgar image is of nuzzling a superior's backside.

clue.text: Our revolutionary, capital Eye is after many years, to move to the right, possibly

definitions.note: the London Eye, the big observation wheel in the capital, is something that revolves

parts.note: a millennium is a thousand years, so many years

parts.words: to move to the right, possibly
parts.note: to wheel is to turn, as in the drill order to wheel right

explanation.surface: Private Eye, after many years, declares itself a revolutionary that may now be drifting rightward politically.
explanation.walkthrough: The London Eye was first called the Millennium Wheel. 'Revolutionary' and 'move to the right' sound political, but they describe a wheel turning.
explanation.definitionFit: The London Eye in the capital was built for the year 2000 and rotates, so it is a revolving Eye.

clue.text: Tabloid editor abandoned his last erection in the main

indicators.note: abandoned means the named letter is dropped from the editor's name

parts.note: Piers Morgan edited the Daily Mirror, a tabloid

indicators.note: last asks for the final letter of the word his

parts.note: the final letter of his is S

explanation.surface: A tabloid editor gave up the last thing he built out at sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'His last' is S, the final letter of 'his', and 'abandoned' drops it from PIERS. The definition is the Eye's smutty joke: a structure put up over the sea ('the main').
explanation.definitionFit: A pier is a structure built out over the sea, which is poetically called the main.

clue.text: Earth electricity supply? Not modern Britain!

definitions.note: a noun phrase describing what Britain once was but no longer is

parts.note: the Earth is the world
power is the electricity supplied to homes

explanation.surface: Wiring a plug to earth, with a dig at Britain's decline.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Earth' looks like the electrical sense, wiring to ground, but it means the planet.
explanation.definitionFit: Britain was a leading global nation with an empire, which it no longer is today.

clue.text: "Sport my ruin" — Hague's unfortunate lot

indicators.note: to ruin the words is to wreck them, so the letters of 'Sport my' are rearranged

explanation.surface: A cry of despair from William Hague about the people he led.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ruin' tells you to rearrange the letters of 'Sport my'. William Hague led the Conservatives after their crushing 1997 defeat, with a much-reduced band of MPs.
explanation.definitionFit: Hague's followers in Parliament were the Conservative members, a group that had little luck at the time.

clue.text: Means of getting shot of a distant celebrity?

definitions.text: Means of getting shot of a distant celebrity?

parts.words: Means of getting shot of a distant celebrity?
parts.note: reads as a way to get rid of a famous person, but describes a camera attachment for photographing someone far away

explanation.walkthrough: 'Getting shot of' usually means getting rid of; here it is taking a photograph of a celebrity from a distance, as paparazzi do.
explanation.definitionFit: This long camera lens magnifies far-off subjects, the paparazzi's tool for photographing famous people from afar.

clue.text: Hunts go around as one means of bagging a fox

indicators.note: around means the letters of 'Hunts go' are moved about into a new order

explanation.surface: Fox hunters ride about, and one way to catch the fox is mentioned.
explanation.definitionFit: A gun loaded with pellets is one way of killing a fox, rather than chasing it with hounds.

clue.text: TV announcer gets to couple with crew

parts.note: to couple things is to link them
to crew a boat is to man it

explanation.surface: A television presenter pairs up with the production team.
explanation.definitionFit: A linkman is the presenter who introduces items on a broadcast and joins them together.

clue.text: Armed Services' policy towards gays: penetration forbidden

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the British forces then banned gay people from serving
second meaning: a sign telling people they may not go in

explanation.walkthrough: The British armed forces banned gay people from serving until 2000; the second meaning is the Eye's crude joke about it.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is the standard sign barring access to a place, and summed up the military ban.

clue.text: Ulster right with Morrison on getting a perfect state?

parts.note: NI is Northern Ireland, often called Ulster
Van Morrison is the singer from Belfast

explanation.surface: Northern Ireland, with its right-wing parties and Van Morrison, reaching an ideal condition.
explanation.definitionFit: Nirvana is the Buddhist ideal of release from suffering, so a blissful condition.

clue.text: Sounds like the car sporting event for the tobacco promoter

indicators.note: Sounds like tells us the answer is said the same as a word for the event

parts.note: a rally is a motor-racing event on public roads

explanation.surface: A motor race named for its tobacco sponsor, as F1 and rallying then were.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sounds like' points to a word said like 'rally'. Sir Walter Raleigh popularised tobacco in England, and his name can be pronounced that way.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Walter Raleigh is credited with bringing tobacco smoking into fashion at the Elizabethan court.

clue.text: Retracts promises, making Blair, according to the Eye, all right on two points

parts.note: Private Eye portrayed Blair as the vicar of St Albion's parish, so he is a Rev
OK means all right
E and S are two compass points

explanation.surface: Blair goes back on his word yet the Eye calls him a decent sort.
explanation.walkthrough: Private Eye ran a column presenting Blair as the trendy vicar of St Albion's, so he is the Rev.
explanation.definitionFit: To revoke a promise is to cancel or withdraw it, so revokes means retracts.

clue.text: Netanyahu possibly makes our PM blow his top

definitions.text: Netanyahu possibly makes our PM blow his top

parts.words: Netanyahu possibly makes our PM blow his top
parts.note: Netanyahu is one example of a citizen of Israel, and the rest is a topical gibe about him angering Blair

explanation.walkthrough: Binyamin Netanyahu was Israel's prime minister in the late 1990s; 'possibly' marks him as one example. The rest of the clue is comment rather than wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Netanyahu is a national of Israel, so he is an example of someone from that country.

clue.text: Place to live round as a working-class type

parts.note: PL is the street-name abbreviation for Place

indicators.note: round means the two letters for living are turned about

parts.note: to be is to live or exist

explanation.surface: A council house as a sign of a person's social class.
explanation.definitionFit: Pleb, from plebeian, is a disparaging word for a common person of low social standing.

clue.text: John has to pucker lips revealing what Brenda and co, get out of taxpayers

definitions.text: what Brenda and co, get out of taxpayers

parts.note: a john is a toilet, as is a privy
to purse your lips is to pucker them

explanation.surface: John makes a face that gives away the cost of the royal family.
explanation.walkthrough: Brenda is Private Eye's nickname for the Queen. The privy purse is the sovereign's income for private expenses.
explanation.definitionFit: The privy purse is the money allowance that pays the monarch's private spending, a royal revenue.

clue.text: Jowell enticed another woman inside

indicators.note: inside, at the clue's end, says the woman's name sits within the words Jowell enticed

parts.note: the letters run across the end of Jowell and the start of enticed

explanation.surface: Tessa Jowell lures a second woman indoors.
explanation.walkthrough: Tessa Jowell was a Labour minister. 'Inside' at the end tells you the woman sits within 'Jowell enticed', across the end of the name and the start of the next word.
explanation.definitionFit: Ellen is a woman's first name, a different woman from Jowell.

clue.text: Pointless s.o.b

parts.note: with its full stops (points) removed, s.o.b. becomes the plain word sob, which means to cry

explanation.walkthrough: S.O.B. looks like the insult, but drop the dots and it is the ordinary verb sob.
explanation.definitionFit: To sob is to cry noisily, and to weep is to shed tears, so they are synonyms.

clue.text: Really suffering, being corporately stretched

definitions.meaning: first meaning: in great distress, as in the idiom
second meaning: having your body literally stretched on the torture rack

explanation.walkthrough: 'Corporately' looks like it is about companies, but here it means bodily.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for anguish comes from the medieval torture device that stretched a victim's body.

clue.text: See 11
Hall, MP — oily, crooked one

indicators.note: crooked means bent out of shape, so these letters are put in a new order

parts.note: A means one

explanation.surface: A greasy, dishonest Member of Parliament named Hall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hall' looks like the MP's surname but is the definition; 'crooked' rearranges MP, OILY and A.
explanation.definitionFit: Olympia is a large exhibition venue in West London, so it is a hall.

clue.text: Primarily stupid, exaggerated, ranting bollocks associated with Paisley's tongue

indicators.note: Primarily tells us to take the first letter of each of the next four words

parts.note: the first letters of these four words spell S, E, R and B
Ian Paisley was the firebrand Ulster unionist leader, so Paisley's first name is IAN

explanation.surface: A rant at the way Ian Paisley talks.
explanation.definitionFit: Serbian is the language of Serbia, and a tongue is another word for a language.
